To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The larvae of red sea brem were fed with rotifers from 3 to15 DAH followed with Artemia nauplin from 16 to40 DAH.
the red sea bream digestive system develops from 3 DAH with the mouth opening, and the enzyme activities and related gene expressions are fluctuated throughout the development.
red sea bream digestive enzymes and gene expression increased with larval development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogenetic developmental of digestive system, digestive enzyme activity and gene expressions of red-sea bream.
the ontogeny of the digestive tract, enzyme activity and gene expressions in larvae of red sea brem.
the ontogenetic digestive development of red sea brem larvae from hatching until metamorphosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the digestive system of red sea brem larvae developed in an order of mouth, pharynx, esophagus, intestine, stomach, pancreas, liver and gallbladder and enzyme activity and gene expressions of digestive enzymes increased and fluctuated during the development.
the digestive tract of red sea brem larvae is functional from hatching to 40 DA, with the digestive enzymes trypsin, lipase, chymotripsin and amylase present and detectable at 3 DAH.
the red sea bream gut is undifferentiated and inactive until the larvae begin to exogenous feeding at 3 DAH and the larvae are capable to digest and absorb the food at 5 DA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ontogenetic digestive development and digestive enzyme activity and related expression in red sea larvae are similar to other marine fish larvae, however the timing of the events are different.
the digestive system of the red sea bream was developed and functional from 5 DAH, which is the time that the larvae started feeding with rotifers and Artemia nauplius.

red sea bream undergoes a complete metamorphosis from yolk sac to exogenous feeding stage, which is accompanied by the differentiation of digestive organs and the increase of digestive enzyme activity and gene expressions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digestive enzyme activity and gene expressions were correlated with the development of digestive tract and the feeding regime.

the digestive enzymes and genes expression were detected during yolk-sac stage, and that enzyme activity and gene expressions of trypsin and chymotryp-sin were higher in larvae fed with DHA enriched rotifers than larvae fed without DHA enriched rotifer.

red sea bream is able to utilize a wide variety of diets during the early developmental stages, and the larval digestive system undergoes a series of morphological, physiological and biochemical changes during larval development.
